title: Recurrent headaches
transcript:
Doctor: Tell me about the headaches.
Patient: They're on one side, throbbing, and I feel sick with them. I get maybe six or seven a month now. Light really bothers me.
Doctor: What have you tried so far?
Patient: I was on sumatriptan, but I stopped it about two months ago because it made my chest feel tight. Now I just take ibuprofen and lie down in the dark.
Doctor: Any other medical problems? Asthma?
Patient: No asthma. I'm otherwise healthy.
Doctor: Any allergies?
Patient: None.
Doctor: Your blood pressure is 118 over 74 and your neurological exam is normal. These sound like migraines. With this many attacks, I'd recommend a daily preventive medication. Let's start propranolol 40 mg once a day. Please keep a headache diary. For attacks, ibuprofen 400 mg is fine, but no more than 10 days a month, to avoid rebound headaches.
Patient: OK.
Doctor: Let's follow up in six weeks. If you get the worst headache of your life or weakness on one side of your body, go straight to the emergency department.
